text.p: Digital Equipment Corp alleged in court papers filed in California on Wednesday that Intel Corp has wielded "monopoly power" by demanding the return of documents which are routinely supplied to computer makers.
"Intel is unlawfully wielding monopoly power in the markets for microprocessors and related products," Digital said in the papers filed in the U.S. District Court in San Jose.

Digital also alleged that Intel is "acting in bad faith and in violation of antitrust law" by demanding the return of documents about the design of Merced, Intel's next generation family of microprocessoers, according to the papers.
Digital said Intel was using its power to harm Digital for selling a competing microprocessor, the 64-bit Alpha chip.

In a footnote, Digital said Intel has a market share "approaching 90 percent" in the domestic and global market for microprocessors, and is trying to "retain that market share and the power that market share gives it."
Earlier this week, Digital said it agreed to return the documents to Intel and had no plans on helping the chip company develop the Merced microprocessor.

The fight over the documents arose after Digital sued Intel in May, alleging the chip-maker stole key semiconductor secrets from it and had infringed on a handful of Digital patents. Intel retaliated by suing to recover the documents..
"Intel filed this action as a vexatious and frivolous ploy in retaliation for Digital's patent infringement action," the court papers said.
